design_references.claim: Cyclomatic complexity = decision points + 1; measures testability, not understandability.
design_references.source: Thomas J. McCabe, 'A Complexity Measure', IEEE TSE SE-2(4), 1976. Recommended module threshold 10 (NIST allows up to 15 with written justification).

design_references.claim: Cognitive Complexity: +1 per flow break, PLUS a nesting increment per level of nesting; else/elsif increment but receive no nesting penalty (the mental cost was paid at the if).
design_references.source: G. Ann Campbell, 'Cognitive Complexity — a new way of measuring understandability', SonarSource v1.7 (2023), Appendix B specification. Peer-reviewed companion: Campbell, TechDebt 2018, doi 10.1145/3194164.3194186.

design_references.claim: Business logic is best understood by slicing around business VARIABLES (what determines this value?), not by listing branch conditions in isolation.
design_references.source: Weiser, 'Program Slicing' (ICSE 1981); COBREX (ICSME 2022) applies exactly this to legacy business-rule extraction — it collects each business variable's statements plus their controlling context statements via DFS over the CFG.

design_references.claim: A COMMIT inside a cursor loop is a recognised Oracle anti-pattern ('incremental commit' / 'fetch across commit') and a first-order migration hazard.
design_references.source: Oracle practitioner literature on ORA-01555 'snapshot too old': committing inside the loop frees undo that the still-open cursor needs, making the error MORE likely, not less. Apache Spark has no transactional equivalent at all.

design_references.claim: The Maintainability Index is deliberately not used.
design_references.source: van Deursen, 'Think Twice Before Using the Maintainability Index' — Halstead Volume has no consensual definition, the formula is dominated by file length, and averaging complexity erases the power-law outliers that carry the actual risk.

note_on_no_internal_callers: Informational only, NOT confirmed dead code — PL/SQL objects are routinely invoked by schedulers, other schemas, or application code entirely outside this repository.
